title: An Asymptotically Sharp Form of the Overfull Conjecture
source_identification: The filename and SHA256 identify the exact reviewed TeX source. No manuscript text is reproduced in this repository.

specifications.scope: The main asymptotic assertion, formulated for labelled finite simple graphs on Fin n, existence of a proper edge coloring with maxDegree colors, and absence of overfull induced vertex sets.

The full assertion of Proposition 7.1 for every odd Delta >= 3: a connected simple graph on Fin (4*Delta+5), maximum degree Delta, no proper Delta-edge-coloring, a proper (Delta+1)-edge-coloring, no Delta-overfull vertex set, and exactly 2*Delta*(Delta+1) edges. The two coloring statements express the exact class-2 conclusion without invoking Vizing’s theorem.

additional_complete_results.scope: For every real c < 1/4 and every natural order bound N, a connected simple class-2 graph exists on Fin n for some n >= N, with maximum degree at least c*n and no overfull vertex set at its maximum degree.

Construct the full actual foreign-edge reduction with constants before the graph: an original-host sequence of pairwise edge-disjoint perfect matchings, its exact regular non-overfull residual with factor-256 degree reserve, actual surviving robust cores and partition, at most three core losses and exceptional additions, and the stated total exceptional unassigned-core incidence bound.

Full Proposition 4.10 with the robust output parameter fixed before every positive requested final error. The original error tolerance and order threshold precede all graph data. The constructed result also satisfies the requested combined final core-error and exceptional-order bound and retains a linear lower bound on every actual final core.

Full Proposition 4.12. Construct actual perfect-matching deletions from the regular non-overfull robust-core partition and total foreign-incidence bound. The exact regular non-overfull residual retains at least three quarters of the original degree, has enlarged robust cores, and has a bounded remaining exceptional set. The positive robust output precedes every arbitrary positive function f. The exceptional bound, positive initial error, and order threshold precede all graph data. The final core error is at most f(|Z_final|) times the actual residual degree, with no monotonicity assumption on f. Lemma 4.13 is proved separately; the terminal factorization and manuscript main theorem remain unverified.

Full Lemma 4.13. From a simple regular non-overfull graph with three or four robust cores and at most t exceptional vertices, construct actual perfect-matching deletions and absorb every exceptional vertex. The exact residual has no overfull set after every prefix, degree h >= k/(3*b4(t)), and disjoint enlarged robust cores covering all vertices. The positive output robustness is chosen before every requested relative error delta>0; the positive initial tolerance and order threshold precede all graph data. The actual final core error and h-r0 are at most delta*h. In the four-odd-part case the actual label forest is a perfect matching or three-edge star, every forest pair has at least r0 actual joining edges, and every union of parts satisfies the forest-cut supply. This reduction supplies no terminal one-factorization; Lemmas 4.14-4.15, Proposition 4.16, and the manuscript main theorem remain unverified.
